# Rework round 4 — claims (alterations_and_tailoring)

- R3-1 / T1-6 (extra_fitting_fee, fitting_number_basis) → the step tier, which reduced to the flat tier on the first two fittings, is gone. The three forms are now: the fee times the fitting number when the ticket has no needed-by date (open-ended fitting rounds); the fee plus a percentage of the ticket's operation charges when the needed-by date is today or within the near window (a late fitting re-checks the whole job); and the flat fee when the needed-by date is further out or already passed. Each pair of tiers gives a different figure on a concrete input of the other tier's domain, and no tier's formula reproduces another tier on that tier's whole domain.
- Class closure for every method factor (rush_charge_basis_form, member_waiver_form, deposit_form_by_record, lined_work_basis_form, quote_tolerance_form, complimentary_waiver_form, fitting_number_basis) → a pairwise table is recorded in the worklog: for each pair of tiers, one input in each tier's domain where the two formulas differ. member_waiver_form is now stated as three tiers (co-pay form, per-operation form, and otherwise the standard method), so its "whole" and "nothing" cases are the standard method rather than two tiers.
- O-R3-1 (pre_work_deposit per-operation form vs "at least deposit_min_usd") → the per-operation form now carries the deposit minimum and the standing-charge cap in both the rule sentence and the compute, matching the overwrite text.
- O-R3-2 (second qualifying operation on a ticket) → the complimentary override now states that any further qualifying operation on the ticket stays chargeable. No case is left to a rule without a booking tool.
- O-8 (escalation only without a needed-by date) → the rule now gives the business reason for each form. Escalation by fitting number applies to tickets with no date to work to. Tickets with a near date pay a share of the job instead; tickets with a distant or passed date pay the flat fee.
- Probe: first-match card reads → every cardmember tier (rush fee, deposit, fitting credit, overrun tolerance) now tests whether the customer holds an active Elite or World Elite account, or any active account. The complimentary card window tests whether the purchase's card account is an active account of the customer. A closed card or a second active card cannot change a tier; decoy probes leave every figure unchanged.
- Probe: first-match registry reads → the occasion rush discount tests for an active registry on the needed-by date, preferring a Wedding Registry. The fitting fee's proximity surcharge and wedding-party credit read the active Wedding Registry (one registry per type), with an active Anniversary or Celebration Registry as the second party-credit tier. Cancelled-registry and second-registry decoys leave every figure unchanged.
- Probe: latest-operation read (lining) → when several operation charges share the latest booking date, the higher one is priced. A ticket with no operation charge owes no lining charge. A same-date decoy operation leaves the lining figure unchanged.
- Probe: absent records and edges → each policy was run with no card account, no membership, no registry, no purchase link, no needed-by date and no charges. Every policy takes its fall-through tier without error. Date differences are guarded against missing dates; a passed needed-by date falls to the flat-fee tier; no read value is ever a divisor.
- Tasks → both worlds and every scored value are unchanged. Proof fields in both tasks were re-swept to the new rule wording (ladder names, tier labels, closure notes).
